guideTitle: Best Folding Pruning Saws for Branches (2026)
metaTitle: Best Folding Pruning Saws for Trees
metaDescription: Compare six folding pruning saws by blade length, curve, teeth per inch, steel, lock and handle, with advice on which branch sizes each saw really handles.
expertTake: The Corona RazorTOOTH 10 inch curved saw is the top pick because its curved blade keeps more teeth in the cut and it locks open for safe work on overhead branches. The Bahco Laplander is the pick for a compact saw that carries in a pocket. Skip the category if your branches are thicker than about 4 or 5 inches, because a folding hand saw tires you out and a pole saw or chain saw is the safer tool.
introParagraphs: A folding pruning saw is a short, aggressive handsaw whose blade folds into the handle, which makes it safe to carry and easy to keep in a bag or on a belt. It cuts on the pull stroke, which gives control when you are cutting branches overhead.

Pruning shears and loppers stop at about an inch or two, and a folding saw covers the gap up to branches several inches thick. The details that matter are blade length and curve, tooth pattern, lock design and handle comfort. This guide compares those.

products.name: Corona RazorTOOTH RS16150B 10 in Curved Folding Pruning Saw

specList.label: Lock
specList.value: Lock-back that holds the blade open

products.description:
The Corona RazorTOOTH RS16150B has a 10 inch curved steel blade, a lock-back folding mechanism and a contoured non-slip handle. The listing explains that the curve keeps more teeth engaged with each stroke, which makes the saw cut faster than a straight blade of the same length.

The tradeoff is price. It is the eleventh most expensive of the twelve candidates, and the 10 inch blade is bulkier to carry than the 7 inch models. Compared with the Corona 7 inch version, it has more reach for thicker limbs. Compared with the Bahco Laplander, it is larger and more aggressive, but it will not fit in a pocket.

In ownership, wipe sap off the blade after use, oil the pivot and keep a sheath or the folded handle closed when carrying. The teeth are hardened and cannot be sharpened with a file, so plan to replace the saw or blade eventually.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who prune thicker branches and want a lock-back curved blade.
pros: Curved 10 inch blade keeps more teeth in the cut for faster sawing
Lock-back design holds the blade firmly open for overhead work
Contoured non-slip handle stays secure in wet or muddy hands
Corona is a long-established garden tool brand with good parts support
cons: Eleventh of twelve in price, near the top of the group
Ten inch blade is too bulky to carry in a pocket

products.name: Bahco Laplander 7.5 in Folding Saw with XT Toothing
products.description:
The Bahco Laplander is a 7.5 inch folding saw with XT toothing at 7 teeth per inch and a safety lock that holds the blade in both the open and closed positions. The listing says it is built for trail maintenance and for green and dry wood, and it packs down small.

The tradeoff is reach and price. A 7.5 inch blade limits you to smaller limbs, and it is the tenth most expensive of the twelve candidates. Compared with the Corona 10 inch, it is easier to carry and less tiring on small cuts but slower on thick wood. Compared with the Fiskars 7 inch, it has a longer blade and a more refined tooth pattern.

In ownership, the lock is the key part: check that it engages fully before each cut. Clean sap with a rag and a drop of oil, and replace the blade when the teeth are dull. The Laplander design is a long-running classic among trail and garden users.
products.bestFor: Gardeners and hikers who want a small, well-made saw for limbs a few inches thick.
pros: Safety lock holds the blade both open and closed for secure carry and use
XT toothing at 7 TPI is designed for fast, clean cuts through wood and brush
7.5 inch blade folds small enough to carry in a pocket or pack
Ergo grip is comfortable for repeated pruning strokes
cons: Tenth of twelve in price, which is high for a 7.5 inch saw
Shorter blade is slower and more tiring on thicker branches

products.name: Fiskars 7 in Folding Hand Saw with Power Tooth Blade
products.description:
The Fiskars folding hand saw has a 7 inch Power Tooth blade with triple-ground teeth, intended to cut wood faster than a plain tooth pattern. The listing describes steel blades that stay sharp through heavy use.

The tradeoff is length and detail. A 7 inch blade handles branches up to a few inches but is slow on thick limbs, and the listing gives less detail about the handle and lock than the Bahco does. Compared with the Corona 7 inch, it is a similar saw from a well-known brand, in the middle of the price order at eighth of twelve. Compared with the REXBETI 8 inch, it is slightly shorter.

In ownership, wipe off sap, keep the blade lightly oiled and check the lock engages. A small saw like this is a good addition to a garden bucket for cutting shrubs and small limbs, but not a substitute for a longer saw on large trees.
products.bestFor: General garden pruning of shrubs and limbs up to a few inches.
pros: Power Tooth triple-ground blade is designed for fast cutting through wood
7 inch folding size is easy to keep in a garden bucket or tool bag
Brand has wide availability and replacement part support
Eighth of twelve in price, mid-range for a branded saw
cons: Seven inch blade is slow on thicker limbs
Listing gives limited detail on the handle and lock design

products.name: REXBETI 11 in Folding Saw with 7 TPI Staggered Teeth, SK5 Steel
products.description:
The REXBETI 11 inch folding saw uses an SK5 steel blade with 7 TPI staggered teeth, and the listing says it cuts branches up to 6 or 7 inches. It is marketed for camping and survival as well as pruning.

The tradeoff is that the capacity claim is the maker's and the saw is a budget-priced design. A 6 to 7 inch branch is a lot of work for any hand saw, and a long blade has more flex. Compared with the Corona 10 inch, it is cheaper at fifth of twelve against eleventh, but the handle and lock are less detailed. Compared with the REXBETI 8 inch, it reaches further.

In ownership, check that the lock is secure and the blade does not wobble. SK5 steel is a high-carbon steel that can rust if left wet, so wipe and oil after use. It is a good value saw for a gardener who wants reach without a high price.
products.bestFor: Budget-minded gardeners who want a long blade for thicker branches.
pros: Eleven inch blade gives more reach and stroke length than the 7 inch saws
SK5 high-carbon steel with 7 TPI staggered teeth is aggressive on green wood
Fifth of twelve in price, much lower than the Corona 10 inch
Folds compactly for a backpack, tool bag or garden shed
cons: The 6 to 7 inch branch capacity is the maker's claim and is tiring in practice
SK5 carbon steel can rust if stored wet, so it needs wiping and oiling

products.name: HURRICANE 10 in Folding Hand Saw with 0.9 mm SK5 Blade
products.description:
The HURRICANE 10 inch folding saw uses a 0.9 mm thick SK5 blade with triple-cut razor teeth at 7 TPI, high-frequency hardened teeth and a chrome electrophoretic finish that the listing says reduces friction in deep cuts.

The tradeoff is brand backing. It is the second cheapest of the twelve candidates and the maker is less established than Corona or Bahco. Compared with the Corona 10 inch, it costs much less and gives a similar blade length. Compared with the REXBETI 11 inch, it is slightly shorter but lists a thickness and finish.

In ownership, a thicker blade resists bending in deep cuts, and the finish helps the blade release sap. Still wipe it after use and oil the pivot. Check the lock before each cut, as lower-priced saws vary in lock quality.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want a long, thick blade at a very low price.
pros: Second lowest price among twelve candidates for a 10 inch saw
Listing states a 0.9 mm blade thickness, which helps resist flex
Chrome electrophoretic finish is described as reducing friction in deep cuts
Triple-cut hardened teeth at 7 TPI cut aggressively on green wood
cons: Less established brand, so lock and pivot quality are less certain
Hardened teeth cannot be resharpened and the blade must be replaced

products.name: LAGOM 11.4 in Curved Folding Pruning Saw, SK5, 3-Gear Lock
products.description:
The LAGOM is an 11.4 inch curved folding saw with an SK5 steel blade and a three-gear lock that holds the blade in several positions. The listing says it is made in Taiwan, and it is the most expensive of the twelve candidates.

The tradeoff is price. You pay the most for a saw that cuts in the same way as the cheaper SK5 models. Compared with the Corona 10 inch, it has a longer blade and a three-gear lock, but costs more still. Compared with the REXBETI 11 inch, it is curved and better finished, but far more expensive.

In ownership, a three-position lock lets you set the blade at an angle for awkward cuts, which is a real convenience. Wipe sap, oil the pivot and avoid forcing the blade in a curved cut. The long curved blade suits thicker branches, but it is also the bulkiest folding saw in the group.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want a long curved blade and a multi-position lock and will pay for it.
pros: Three-gear lock holds the blade open at several angles for awkward cuts
11.4 inch curved SK5 blade is the longest in the group for thick limbs
Made in Taiwan, which some buyers prefer for build consistency
Secure lock also holds the blade closed for safe carrying
cons: Most expensive of the twelve candidates by a clear margin
Longest blade makes it the bulkiest saw to carry and store

buyingCriteria.explanation: Blade length sets how thick a limb you can cut without sawing in a cramped stroke. Seven inches handles branches up to about 3 inches, and 10 to 11 inches handle 4 or 5 inches more comfortably. Listing claims of 6 or 7 inches, as on the REXBETI, are possible but tiring. Match the blade to your typical limb.

A curved blade, like the Corona 10 inch or the LAGOM, keeps more teeth engaged with each pull and cuts faster. A straight blade, like the Fiskars, is easier to use in tight spots. Curved is better for open limbs, and straight is better for flush cuts against a trunk.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Teeth per inch and tooth pattern
buyingCriteria.explanation: Most folding saws use about 7 TPI with triple-ground or staggered teeth. Fewer TPI cuts green wood faster and rougher, and more TPI cuts smoother and slower. The Bahco uses XT toothing and the Fiskars uses Power Tooth. Pattern matters more than a small TPI difference.

A folding saw must lock open or it can close on your fingers. The Corona uses a lock-back, the Bahco has a safety lock for open and closed, and the LAGOM has a three-gear lock. Check the lock by pulling and pushing the blade before the first cut.

SK5 high-carbon steel is common and holds an edge, but it can rust. The HURRICANE lists a 0.9 mm blade, which resists flex in deep cuts. Thin blades bend and thick blades cut slower. Most hardened teeth cannot be resharpened, so plan for replacement.

You push and pull a saw many times, so grip matters. Look for a contoured, non-slip handle, as on the Corona, and a guard if possible. Wear gloves and eye protection when cutting overhead, and never cut with the blade above your shoulders on a ladder.

specDecoder.meaning: The cutting length of the blade when open. A longer blade gives a longer stroke and handles thicker limbs.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Fiskars is 7 inches, the Bahco 7.5, the HURRICANE 10, the REXBETI 11 and the LAGOM 11.4.

specDecoder.meaning: Teeth per inch sets how coarse the cut is. Lower TPI cuts faster and rougher, and higher TPI cuts slower and smoother.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bahco, REXBETI and HURRICANE all list 7 TPI.

specDecoder.meaning: The steel decides edge life and rust resistance. SK5 is a high-carbon steel that is hard but needs wiping.
specDecoder.watchFor: The REXBETI, HURRICANE and LAGOM list SK5 steel.

specDecoder.meaning: Thickness affects how well the blade resists bending. A thicker blade is stiffer but removes more wood per cut.
specDecoder.watchFor: The HURRICANE lists 0.9 mm, and many listings give no thickness.

specDecoder.meaning: The lock holds the blade open for cutting and closed for carrying. A secure lock is a basic safety feature.
specDecoder.watchFor: The LAGOM uses a three-gear lock, and the Bahco locks both open and closed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade length and curve
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated blade lengths from 7 to 11.4 inches and whether the blade is curved. A curve helps on open limbs. We did not cut with any saw.

howWeEvaluated.title: Teeth and steel
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tooth patterns and steel from the published listings. Most use 7 TPI, and the SK5 models can rust. The Bahco XT and Fiskars Power Tooth are named designs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lock and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at lock designs, since a folding saw that closes mid-cut is a hazard. The Bahco and LAGOM publish their locks in detail.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handle and ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered grips, sap cleanup and wear based on owner feedback patterns. Pivots and locks are the wear parts, and hardened teeth cannot be resharpened.

howWeEvaluated.title: Claims and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We treated branch capacity claims, such as 6 or 7 inches on the REXBETI, as the maker's. We weighed price position against blade length and lock design.

cards.label: Curved blades
cards.text: The Corona 10 inch and LAGOM keep more teeth in the cut, so they cut faster on open limbs. They are bulkier and harder to use flush to a trunk.

cards.label: Straight blades
cards.text: The Fiskars and Bahco are compact and handle tight spots and flush cuts. They are slower on thick limbs.

howToChoose.note: Choose a curved blade for open limbs, and a straight one for tight spots and portability.

rows: Folds compactly despite the long blade

howToChoose.subheading: For Tree and Branch Pruning Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A secure lock, a curved blade of 10 inches or more for thick limbs, and a non-slip grip. Cut with the pull stroke, undercut first to avoid tearing bark, and wear eye protection.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Corona 10 inch is the best all-round saw, and the LAGOM suits the thickest limbs. The Bahco is the pocket option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You prune often, want a secure multi-position lock, or want a known brand with a refined blade and handle, as with the Corona or Bahco.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You prune a few times a year. The HURRICANE and REXBETI give long blades for much less.

maintenance.why: Sap gums the teeth and slows cutting. A rag with a little solvent or oil keeps the blade clean.
High-carbon steel rusts and pivots stiffen. A light oil coat protects both.
A worn lock can let the blade close on your hand. Replace the saw if the lock is loose.
Bent or missing teeth slow cutting and bind. Hardened teeth cannot be sharpened, so replace the blade or saw.
A saw can spread disease from one tree to the next. Wipe the blade with a disinfectant before moving on.

faq.q: Is a curved or straight pruning saw better?
faq.a: Curved blades cut faster on open limbs, while straight blades are easier in tight spots and for flush cuts. Choose by the cuts you make most often.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a folding pruning saw?
faq.a: Little. The HURRICANE and REXBETI give long blades for less. Pay more for a known brand, a better lock and a comfortable handle.

faq.q: How long do the blades last?
faq.a: Hardened teeth stay sharp for a long time but cannot be resharpened. No listing states a rated life, so plan to replace the saw or blade when it dulls.

faq.q: What size branch can a folding saw cut?
faq.a: Seven inch saws suit up to about 3 inches, and 10 to 11 inch saws handle 4 or 5 inches. Maker claims of 6 or 7 inches are possible but tiring.
It is safe if the lock is secure and you wear gloves and eye protection. Never cut overhead without a firm stance, and keep the saw closed when carrying.
Most have hardened teeth that file sharpening will not fix. Replace the saw or blade when it dulls, and keep the blade clean to maintain cutting speed.
